modules.module_title: Collection and preparation of raw materials and tools

pcs.pc_description: Gather raw materials such as coconuts and husk for coir fibre production.
Gather traditional tools, such as iron rods and hand-beaters, as well as modern machines such as Dehusking machines, Defibering machines, and Refining machines.

Transport any extra materials to the designated storage area to maintain workplace order.

modules.module_title: Coir fibre extraction using traditional methods

pcs.pc_description: Dry coconut shells under sunlight for several days to aid in husk separation.
Soak dried coconut shells in water for over six months to soften the husk.
Remove the coconuts from the water and repeatedly beat them with an iron rod to remove the fibres.
Manually peel off the outer layer to separate the husk.
Bundle the husk and soak it again for further softening.
Use husk bundles in a water tank for two to four days for refinement.
Extract fibres by manually beating the soaked husk or using traditional tools.

modules.module_title: Coir fibre extraction using modern machines

pcs.pc_description: Put the dried coconut shells into a Dehusking machine to separate the husk.
Transfer the husk to a Defibering machine to break it down into finer fibres.
Use a refining machine, locally known as 'kudu,' to remove unwanted particles and extract clean coir fibres.
Roll the refined fibres into bundles for easy handling and transportation.

modules.module_title: Spinning and Twisting of Coir fibre

pcs.pc_description: Strengthen fibres by twisting two strands together using a traditional spinning wheel or a mechanised spinning machine.
Extend the fibre length by joining twine ends through friction or using a mechanised splicing tool.
Bundle the spun coir fibres and prepare large spools for further product manufacturing.

modules.module_title: Product Specification in Coir Product Making

pcs.pc_description: Home décor making in coir involves crafting items like planters, show piece, wall hangings, etc. by shaping quality fibres, adding decorative touches, and ensuring durability.
Coir doormat making involves selecting sturdy fibres, weaving them into a tight, durable mat, adding patterns or borders, and ensuring quality for long-lasting use.
Coir rope weaving involves twisting strong fibres into sturdy strands, providing uniform thickness and durability for various applications.
Coir brush making involves bundling stiff fibres, securing them to a handle, trimming for uniformity, and ensuring durability for effective cleaning.
